text: I had a wonderful experience at Lotus's Bang Pakok on the evening of March 9th. I was purchasing a large amount of items for my new home and needed help with a complex delivery. The manager and his entire team were incredibly professional and friendly—this branch truly sets a high standard for customer service! They made the whole logistics process seamless and stress-free. If you are shopping for a big home project, I highly recommend the Bang Pakok team for their helpfulness and efficiency. Thank you so much!

One-stop for your daily or weekend grocery shopping.  Tesco’s supermarket is quite significant to serve one’s daily needs. It contains a major and standard Thai franchise of restaurants and a decent food court.  But if you are looking for high-end brands shopping for fashion apparel and accessories, this is not a stop. The Cineplex is another highlight for movie entertainment and an arcade corner for tiny kids. I recommend trying the beef soup in the food court area. The bread and pastries at the Yamazaki bakery is great.  Literally, you have everything in one place for kids or office accessories.

text: Stopped by for a bite to eat. Lots of food options.

The staff were chatting amongst themselves, ignoring the customers waiting. They didn't ask us anything, but another customer asked what we needed help with, even though we were waiting first and they didn't ask. What kind of behavior is this? What's the point? Do they really not see us, or are they selective about how they serve customers? There's a sign asking what to write on, but it doesn't specify what to write on. Are customers supposed to figure it out themselves? Another customer asked, and they were told. I'm very confused about this. None of them looked welcoming; are they just going through the motions at work?

The downstairs restroom is filthy, the urinal is broken and hasn't been fixed for months. You have to wait to use the restroom if you need to urinate. They only care about selling products. It's inconvenient for elderly people; they'd rather go to Big C.
